Awaiting your direction before proposing one.

row.comment:
Confirmed live, not theoretical: escalations_old has completed rows at id=1,3,4 ('hypocrisy'/'malice'/'abomination' registrations); the live escalation table's sqlite_sequence is currently at 4 (reset during today's rebuild testing per BUILD.md sec161: 'id sequences reset again, live tables left empty and ready for real use'), so 'escalation #4' is now genuinely ambiguous between two different real items. This breaks the id-continuity guarantee escalation-redesign-plan-v1 sec2 deliberately chose ('every existing cross-reference... keeps working') and that cfg_column.escalation.id.use still claims is true ('continues from escalations_old's max (735)'). Proposed fix: reseed escalation's sqlite_sequence to 735 now, while only 4 live rows exist (cheap/safe), before real backlog accumulates on top of the collision. Full detail: iba/docs/escalation-design-plan-v1-20260820.md (tables and columns section).
D1's dry-run phase is built and run (iba/app/migration/rebuild_escalation_from_export_20260821.py --dry-run -> iba/app/reports/escalation-rebuild-dry-run-20260821.md + matching .json). Confirms a reseed-and-replay reproduces every original #7xx id exactly, surfaces 22/25 items' titles as mechanically resolvable (raise with the item's own final corrected title) and 3 (#749/#751/#757) needing an actual new one chosen. Separately: researcher, reviewing the JSON, asked whether #736 being originally on-hold was lost data or a missing conversion -- checked directly against escalations_old: 3 of the 4 carried-over items were genuinely on-hold (#650/#654/#668 -> #736/#737/#738), 1 was in-progress (#725 -> #739). Not lost data (the hold reason survives as prose in context/comment), but the STRUCTURED state column was reset to 'raised' for all 4 at the 2026-08-19/20 cutover -- mechanical, not incidental: raise_new() has no way to create an item at anything other than 'raised' (except the special-cased notice type), so whoever did the cutover was forced into this. The dry run as currently built perpetuates it (copies each item's export state forward unchanged). New decision needed for D1: restore the true original state for these 4 at replay, or deliberately keep them 'raised' matching the cutover's own choice? Execute still not built -- D1's two-phase gate stands.
Researcher spotted v2/v3 of #736 showing the same comment text twice in the JSON. Checked precisely: v3's comment textually CONTAINS v2's comment as a prefix plus a genuinely new appended paragraph -- comment/context are cumulative-append columns (matching live escalation.comment's own semantics), and the dry-run's _diff_versions() was computing the delta as the WHOLE new value instead of just the increment, for these two columns specifically. Fixed: for a clean append (cv starts with pv+'\n'), the increment is extracted so replaying it through update()'s real _append() reproduces the export's own value exactly -- verified with a self-check comparing the simulated reconstruction against the export's own recorded value at every version. That fix then surfaced something much bigger: 22 of the 25 items have at least one version where comment/context was NOT a clean append at all -- a genuine REPLACEMENT (matching the #759 wave's own description, 'prior full text redistributed... per the researcher's column-spec correction'). update() has no replace mode for these fields, only append -- the same underlying limitation as #10's short_description gap, now shown to also cover comment/context. Consequence: for these 22 items, replaying every increment literally through today's real update() would NOT reproduce the true historical value -- it would carry the pre-correction text forward as a permanent, contaminating prefix on every later update. This argues D1 may need a different execute strategy for these items: raise/set the FINAL settled field values directly (v1's history row can hold any values -- it's not append-constrained) rather than faithfully replaying every increment, with the original export JSON (already archived verbatim) serving as the permanent record of the full blow-by-blow narrative for anyone who needs it. Not decided -- your call.

row.short_description: PS scripts bypassing run.py are outside governance
row.comment:
Surfaced investigating the escalation-report registration gap (related to #6, not a subtask of it -- a genuinely separate topic that happened to be found through it). Checked live, not assumed: 45 PS scripts in iba/app/ps. 37 dispatch through run.py (python -m iba.app.run ... --step ... --run-id ...) and get a real run row, run_id, cfg_step registration, and module_blocking protection. 8 do not: Behaviour.ps1, Escalation.ps1, Start-Iba.ps1 (necessarily -- it bootstraps what run.py itself depends on), and five lowercase-hyphenated one-off scripts (create-iba-view-template.ps1, create-passage-view-and-export.ps1, create-passages-by-book-view-and-export.ps1, export-iba-config-tables.ps1, generate-iba-db-schema-report.ps1) that also don't follow the PascalCase naming convention every governed script uses. None of the 8 are registered in cfg_utility either -- checked, cfg_utility has zero .ps1 rows at all; it only tracks the Python modules behind a script, so a script whose underlying operation never goes through run.py leaves no record anywhere that it ran, when, or with what result -- not a partial record, none. Found one case that's worse than a clean bypass: Debate-Run.ps1 dispatches its main step through run.py correctly, then separately calls python -m iba.app.tools.build_debate_report directly afterward -- an ungoverned side-operation tacked onto an otherwise-governed run. escalation.py's own CLI is currently the ONE exception with a hand-built safety net (this session's crash-wrapper, auto-raising a run_error on any uncaught exception) -- every other bypassing script has none. This is the concrete mechanism behind the researcher's own observation: understanding of what the engine records and what's actually happening are apart, because 'governed' currently means 'happens to be registered as a cfg_step', not 'is actually a table property with mechanical guarantee' -- an operation is either wired into run.py or it is invisible, with nothing in between and no signal to tell you which a given script is without checking it directly, the way this investigation just did.
D4/D16/D23 (register v9) fixed the originating case: escalation.list/history now dispatch through run.py (work package escalation-reporting), not a direct module call. The other 7 scripts this item names (Behaviour.ps1, Start-Iba.ps1 -- necessarily -- and 5 lowercase one-off scripts) plus Debate-Run.ps1's ungoverned side-call to build_debate_report are NOT touched this round -- out of scope. Staying open for a decision on the rest.
